statement: Charging a consumer for goods or services sold in an Internet transaction through a negative option feature is unlawful unless the seller provides text that clearly and conspicuously discloses all material terms of the transaction before obtaining the consumer's billing information, obtains the consumer's express informed consent before the charge, and provides simple mechanisms for the consumer to stop recurring charges (15 U.S.C. § 8403(1)-(3)).
caveat: The FTC's 2024 amendments to 16 CFR part 425 (the 'click-to-cancel' requirements) were vacated on judicial review in July 2025 before their compliance date and do not appear in the part in force, which covers prenotification negative option plans; the FTC opened a new rulemaking with an advance notice of proposed rulemaking in March 2026. Several states (including California) impose their own automatic-renewal statutes with independent disclosure and cancellation requirements. This repo does not assess a specific subscription flow.
